items.text: Hello Everyone,
We’re back with a small news between patches to tease what’s coming next to the Spirit Realm.

First of all, thank you so much for all your feedback on Discord, Reddit, and in the comments. It is incredibly valuable for us as we continue to improve the game’s balance and search for the perfect middle ground for you. What truly drives us forward and reassures us that we are on the right path are your reviews, which have been absolutely amazing. We are currently sitting at 92 percent positive reviews, and we are actively working to address your issues and concerns.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45446539/e21b0a2e1f66f9cc938c0e46e6f364368726dc8b.png"]

We also know that some players are struggling with enemy attack patterns and lack of the information about them in the game, which was mainly mentioned in the negative reviews. While we respect your point of view and understand the reasoning behind those negative reviews, making the game this way was a conscious decision on our side. From the very beginning, our goal was to include this layer of difficulty, encouraging players to learn enemy behaviors and rethink how to rebuild their decks after consecutive defeats, without any additional information.
But we do not want to leave you without support!
That is why we created a new “Before You Play” news post on Steam and released a Gameplay Showcase Trailer that offers more insight into how the game works:
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2825880/view/511850776162731286"][dynamiclink href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r2Wtf0_herA"]

In addition, we are constantly collaborating with the community to create guides and an official wiki. It will cover detailed game information, including enemy patterns and statistics, for those of you who want to dive deeper in the mechanics of the game from the very beginning.
At the end, We do not want to spoil too much, but we are preparing something interesting for you. Below, you can find a small glimpse of what we are working on :skull: :skull: :skull: :
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45446539/846e2382a90a41d706f00528f4d55f2aaa143c17.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45446539/bb6d9295d0439e32e7450262d4f8730785c5a4a3.png"]
Don't forget to chat with other souls on our r/DeathHowl subbredit and Discord!
See you soon!
~ The Outer Zone and 11 bit studios Teams
Hello Lost Souls,

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45446539/1c8fa3c73a573b775069d347d90c5878561bc9ba.png"]

‘Bug’ Fylge occasionally bites for 1 dmg, nomnom

Overwhelmed

New audio when getting chilled.

Improved the AI of the Night Leech.
New animation for branch style attacks. (Staff of Thorns card, Thorns totem, Blood card).

Fixed a blocker that happened when you walked away from the Sorg arena after dying.
Cave Painter’s marker (X) is now correctly removed from the map upon completion.
The bridge to the Creek of Spectral Falls is now crumbled on the map after it collapsed.
Fixed bug with the visual effects from Shattering Ground / Infected Molar not disappearing after finishing combat.
Sorg's eyes no longer trigger “Kill” effects.
Fixed cases of crushed Chinese font.
Fixes to the mini boss puzzle in The Breathing Chasm.
Fixed bug resulting in overheal from Crystalized Ox Heart totem.
Fixed bug where the keyword info box had the wrong color in the card manager (when playing with a controller)
Fixed bug where Burning Void would fight against you even though you revived them with the Horned Menace spirit card (very safe to hug now)
Fixed bug where damage text was not updated with the correct damage buff number on the ‘Oppression’ card.
Removed loot drops from Soother and Trunkrot mini bosses.
Fixed Distorted Hollows great spirit memory sequence.
Added more Arrow Gill to the caves of Creek of Spectral Falls so all cards of the Realm of Distorted Hollows can be crafted.
Ro will now helpfully remind players to craft cards if that is something they have forgotten to do after a few battles in a new region.

Additionally, after dying in one of the elite battles before a Great Spirit, Ro might hint to players to git gud get stronger and return later if she senses they need to craft more region cards. Don’t worry, she will not nag.

Added a dedicated controller button to open the overworld map.
Added 'scary roar' events (ooOOoo) when entering a Great Spirit area \[to communicate increased danger/difficulty].
Added hover feedback and blinking on the 'new cards unlocked' pop-up notification.
Improved system for the fold-out menu
When new cards or totems are unlocked, players will see an exclamation point (!) on their tabs and on the fold-out main tab. They disappear after opening the correct tab.
Whenever there are any teardrops to spend, players will see an exclamation mark on the progression tab.
We encourage you to continuously share your feedback in the comments, reviews, and across our community channels. Your suggestions constantly help us improve your experience in the game.
Stay tuned for the upcoming updates!
~ The Outer Zone and 11 bit studios Teams

items.text: Hello Souls!

Thank you so much for all the ongoing feedback shared here and on our Discord, and Reddit. Every voice matters to us, and we’re committed to improving your experience. What was originally planned as a small hotfix has grown into a full-scale patch, and we hope these changes make your adventures in the Spirit Realm even better.
Also, if you haven’t done so yet, please consider leaving a review on Steam, it really helps us a lot!
● Fixed all bugs related to soft locks caused by the Skull Fylge dying on its own.
● Fixed bugs related to Fylge stepping in ooze without dying at 0 health.
● The unattainable Worm Jaw material has been removed, and the materials required to craft the Stinger card have been updated accordingly.
● Corrected an issue where encounters disappeared from the map when opening the map of a location from different realms.
● Fixed the shortcut to the Mountain in the south of The Hidden Vale not being indicated on the map or in the environmental visuals.
● Fixed some block cards not displaying the correct amount of block.
● Fixed an issue where Ro's model could get stuck in spirit form after a fight, causing an incorrect outline to persist.
● Fixed an issue where the player could interact with the trunk immediately after defeating Trunkrot to reacquire the Sinister Twig card.
● Adjusted the Crumbler enemy AI and visuals; also removed the strong attack indicator (!) as it was incorrectly placed.
● Frostgrowl will no longer cough up its heart if doing so would result in its own death, good boy!
● Some early-game arenas have been adjusted so you can get the ball rolling from the start slightly easier now.

● Certain difficult caves have been eased when they were not located next to a sacred grove. We felt that too many caves were not only very hard but also difficult to reach, making them overly punishing.
● More Nests with teardrops have been added to help players who don’t find the minibosses and therefore have too few tears to progress. Nests have been added in the following locations:
○ Meadows of Delusion
○ Shores of Darkness
○ The Hidden Vale
○ The Breathing Chasm
○ Valley of Desolation
○ The Wailing Marshes
○ Cadaver Dunes

● Some overpowered card combos from the Realm of Piercing Winds have been nerfed. Previously, it was too easy to create a combo deck from this realm that could beat The Howling Mountain directly without visiting other realms or defeating other bosses:
○ Exploding Blocks: now removes all block instead of just 3
○ Bracing for Battle: gives 1 mana instead of 2
○ Double Block: costs 1 more mana
○ Harden Soul: costs 1 more mana
○ Overwhelmed mode: now requires 1 additional block to charge in the Realm of Piercing Winds
○ Peak \[Realm of Hostile Plains]: now gives 1 mana instead of 2
○ Algae Bubble: loses 2 health instead of 1
○ Petrified Cheernut: adds a -1 card penalty on top of the existing mana penalty
● The location of Bird (from the Blue Bird quest in the Forest of Howling Shadows) has been moved to another location, but within the same Forest; the trees are nicer there.
● Cards are no longer highlighted when craftable. Instead, a bright border now indicates which cards can be crafted, improving overall readability.
● 'New Cards Unlocked' banner now blinks to improve readability.
See you in the next update!
~ The Outer Zone and 11 bit studios Teams
Hello Lost Souls!
After the release we are coming back to you with small pack of quick fixes which we are introducing today, according to your feedback.
Fixed a bug where unlocking the Special Realm Card before unlocking any other card in that realm did not give access to the realm's Card Panel.
Fixed a bug where the game wouldn’t proceed to the next turn if a Fylge died in the fire from Light a Fire card. Fylge’s remain unafraid of fire.
Fixed VFXs persisting after using certain cards in specific circumstances.
Sobslug telegraphs its attacks correctly now (!).
The player can shoot over Bursting Growth after it has exploded.
Fixed bones showing in Cadaver Dunes while inside a grove.
Fixed some objects In Forest of Howling Shadows showing up while inside arenas.
Fixed Doomglare’s shadow (it is no longer a vampire).
Fixed erratic camera’s movement when entering a cave in The Breathing Chasm.
Fixed the game not proceeding to the next turn when Gnawskull kills the last boar in a secret encounter in The Hidden Vale.
Fixed out-of-bounds issue after talking to the moose in Meadows of Delusion.
Fixed the narwhal tooth event in The Hidden Vale. You can now click on it again and again (if you want) and the eye icon has been placed better.
Visual fixes for multiple area transitions.
In the coming updates, we will try to make a smoother on-boarding experience, with focus on UI feedback and a better diffuculty curve when entering new areas. We will also do some balancing of caves.
Furthermore, we will try to tackle the biggest bugs and add some QOL here and there.
We want to add some more treats for you, but that will come at a later time.

~ The Outer Zone and 11 bit studios Teams

notes.title: Now let’s immerse ourselves in Spirit Realm

items.text: Ro’s Journey Into the Spirit World

So let’s start with our main character - Ro, a mother pushing through grief and decay in search of her lost son, Olvi. Her path winds through thirteen biomes, each filled with unique threats, craftable cards, materials, and over thirty enemy types. Although the world is open for exploration, progression is shaped by combat encounters that block the paths between Sacred Groves - the rare places where Ro can heal, save, and upgrade her abilities.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45446539/95e06a638b7873e4febd0c69533a27002cbe7396.gif"]
Tactical, Turn-Based Combat

Every encounter unfolds on a turn-based, grid-based battlefield. You begin by placing Ro on the grid and planning the first move. Each point of mana (red dots) allows her to move one tile or play a card, creating constant decisions between positioning, offense, and survival.

Enemies respond dynamically to your actions. Some punish careless movement, others exploit gaps in your defense, and all follow patterns you must learn and adapt to. Failure is part of the learning process, and every defeat pushes you toward smarter strategies (much like in Soulslike games!), but this time with cards.

notes.title: Here are some examples of monster moves

items.text: Gloomcroak, which pulls Ro in with its tongue
Slobslug, which poisons and shields itself
Dreadfins, which counter ranged attacks with a piercing dash
Dire Shrooms, which drag Ro closer before striking hard
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45446539/48bf8189bf06ec7b5a630927a3feac349a649ed8.gif"]
Understanding these behaviors and anticipating them will help you achieve victory.

Your deck defines your capabilities. Cards are crafted from world materials (such as rocks, sticks, flora) and the Death Howls earned from enemies. Every card has a cost, effect, and synergy potential, many of which are tied to the biome where you find them. The deck also reflects the consequences of Ro’s journey; certain enemy attacks add Wound cards, and quests may temporarily place items into your draw pool, disrupting your normal play flow.

Death Howl’s combat encourages thoughtful sequencing. Even modest cards can become powerful when combined properly. For example, pairing damage-increasing effects with discard-based attacks can escalate a simple strike into a devastating chain.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45446539/6699aa2558d46c78481c731c6fa392c2ac41da51.gif"]
Sacred Groves, Skills, and Growth
Sacred Groves act as your checkpoints in the hostile world. Here, Ro can recover her health, save progress, and convert collected Howls into Teardrops, the resource used to unlock or upgrade skills.

One such ability is Overwhelmed, which boosts the damage of every card you play during a turn. It becomes especially valuable when draw clutter, such as quest items or Wound cards reduces your options. Strategic use of Overwhelmed can swing difficult battles back in your favor.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45446539/82872ba6a804ea410bb1b4f612dc9c3ed7218a0b.gif"]

Beyond cards and skills, Ro can equip Totems: powerful artifacts that reshape the rhythm of battle. As she gains experience, additional Totem slots unlock, allowing you to strategize your play flow even further..

For example: The Pearl Totem, shown in the gameplay video, lets you discard cards during combat and gain Block equal to their cost. Items like this reinforce the idea that skills, decks, and Totems operate together as a flexible combo.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45446539/2651a256b7693656a30f4c40258a59c033287158.gif"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45446539/52da24466a36aa1df8187dfc95cf04ffe43e3c21.gif"]
We think we have explained the most important mechanics so far here, and now Death Howl’s world is on the horizon, and we can’t wait for you to experience it!
~ The Outer Zone and 11 bit studios Teams
Greetings, Lost Souls!

We can proudly say that our adventures with Ro are taking more shape than ever. We are almost ready to announce the release date, but we need to keep you waiting a little bit longer. And yes, we are still on track to release Death Howl in 2025!
13 locations, 24 different types of enemies, around 150 different cards, quests, and many more features unlockable through story progression is almost done at the moment.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45446539/71d0e5a75587324e01a786978b924de0d65f1337.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45446539/f82f1e633e2e2ec6c569518647f9ef24b3fcd109.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45446539/a26f4f30d608b63027437377d482fdf2ae53bf40.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45446539/80a61d34c44488475e3256c1fb655bb6869a3a65.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45446539/11f8e7d3af22aacfa6da9d7f144f10469dafba9e.png"]

To help you get more familiar with the mechanics and gameplay awaiting you in the full release, we have prepared a new Gameplay Showcase Trailer, where we break down all the important things you need to know while playing Death Howl.

notes.title: Our trailer is divided into 5 parts

items.text: “Balancing The Scales” – An example of a quest appearing in a location and how it affects gameplay.
Cards, Crafting & Upgrading Skills – As your story progresses, you will find materials to upgrade your deck. Here, you will learn how to do it.
Combat Basics – Combat is a major part of the game, and here you will find everything you need to get started.
Advanced Combat Strategies – Combos, synergies, and environment interactions that will help you defeat stronger enemies.
Spirit Cards & Totems – A skill tree with powerful boons that enhance your deck’s power.
In the next announcements, we are planning to prepare a whole article series for you, which will serve as a guide when you need help or want to learn more about the game’s mechanics.
Sign up for the Playtests this weekend!
As we have almost everything set, we would like to make sure that everything is balanced to your future journeys
That’s why we are opening sign-ups for the closed playtests of Death Howl which will be held from November 7th to 10th.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45446539/9580cb70236f071153ec761d15af34bc214417af.png"]
To sign up, just click a button on the Steam Store Page, and you are all set!
During the playtests, you will be able to experience most of the content that will be available in the final release of the game (around 20+ hours of it), both on PC and Steam Deck!
We will appreciate all of your feedback and cannot wait to see you in the Spirit Realm.
Take care,
~ 11 bit studios and The Outer Zone teams
Hello Wanderers,

We’re excited to bring you our first big Development Update for Death Howl in which we would like to show you some nice sneak peaks and updates. The whole team (well, the three of us here in Denmark) are working hard on the game and things are going smoothly! The official release date announcement is getting closer, but before all that, check out the brand new Gameplay and Demo!:
First off, a huge thank you for all the amazing feedback on the demo! Your support has been incredibly motivating and keeps us pushing forward.

We’re happy to announce that we are bringing the demo back starting June 9th, during the upcoming Steam Next Fest - updated, extended, and refined! It’s the perfect time to step back into Ro’s shoes and journey once more into the spirit realm.

notes.title: Enter the “Creek of the Spectral Falls” – a strange new region featuring

items.text: 🦌 New crafting cards and synergies to experiment with
🦌 A boss fight with one of the Great Spirits: Cantharsis
🦌 Core gameplay improvements, including an enhanced progression system

That’s not all! We’ve been feeling a little nostalgic lately and stumbled upon some early production phase gems we’d love to share with you. Below, you’ll find a selection of early concept sketches of the in-game map and locations as well as key art, and brainstorm assets from the very beginning of Death Howl’s journey. These pieces were created when the idea for the game was just starting to take shape. We hope you’ll enjoy it!:

Thank you once again for your continued support, feedback, and kind words. We hope you will enjoy the new demo even more than the first one and if you do, please consider leaving a review in the comments once it will be available. Every bit of feedback helps us make Death Howl even better!
Death Howl demo will be back starting June 9th, during the upcoming Steam Next Fest, don’t forget to try it!
See you soon in the spirit realm. 🦌
~ The Outer Zone Team

items.text: Hello everyone,
We've just released a small patch to address some of the most frequently reported issues to make sure you have the best possible experience with the demo!
Fixed a bug where completing the burning tree and bird quest still allowed players to pick up the bird in its old spot.
Resolved an issue where an enemy's movement indicator would stick around if they were killed at the exact moment their movement was displayed.
Fixed an issue in the moose tutorial where players could walk completely out of frame.
Polished up Overwhelmed Mode to make it easier to notice and use, with clearer visuals and helpful hints.
Adjusted some terminology for clarity and fixed missing translations where needed.
Smoothed out interactions with healing and fast travel to make things feel more natural.
Fireball got a bit of a buff because, well, it needed more oomph.
Make sure to share your feedback and review the demo. Your input will help us make the best game possible!
Take care,
The Outer Zone team and 11 bit studios
